_readme: The SECOND PriceList, prepared 2026-09-09 and NOT SIGNED. It is a new message on the
price topic, not a replacement for sequence 1: §14.3 selects the price current at a
purchase by the message's own consensus timestamp, so the schedule on consensus is the
sequence of messages and nothing is ever edited. app/price-list.hedera-testnet.json is
left exactly as it is, because priceListStep.confirm rebuilds it and compares it
byte-for-byte against the message at sequence 1.
WHY IT EXISTS. D-159's addendum (2026-09-09) makes the provisioning purchase one atomic
transaction with three legs: hbar from the buyer to the Postmaster for the price,
$POSTAGE from the treasury to the agent's public-key alias, and the registration fee in
hbar from the Postmaster to that same alias. §14.3 requires the Postmaster to publish a
price before charging under it, so the provisioned path cannot be sold until this
message is on the topic. The first PriceList omitted `provisioning` entirely (D-57:
provisioning is never required), which is why this is an addition and not a correction.
WHAT IS UNFILLED, AND BY WHOM.
stampToken.tokenId       filled from app/deployment/hedera-testnet.json at submission,
stampToken.treasury      exactly as the first message's were. They exist now, and they
methods[].payTo          are not written here because the submitting script is their
single source and the two must not drift.
WHAT IS FILLED, AND ON WHAT WARRANT.
provisioning.method             'hbar'. The x402-usdc purchase leg is deferred this
window and LIMITATIONS L-11 names our scoping as the
reason, so the provisioned path is offered on the leg
that is built.
provisioning.unitPrice          '2'. RECORD (Sonic, 2026-09-09): two hbar flat for the
mailbox purchase, priced in hbar with NO rate. His
reasoning, recorded because the number is only as good
as it: every cost the Postmaster incurs for provisioning
is denominated in hbar — the 2026-09-09 HIP-542 probe
measured account creation at 0.64 hbar plus the
transfer's own fee, and each topic creation is likewise
hbar — so a flat hbar price is stable against the rate
in a way a USDC-referenced one is not, and for the MVP
that is the right kind of stable.
Note what this does NOT change: the stamp's own price.
§14.3 lets a method be priced by unitPrice OR by rate,
never both, and that pipe is exclusive per METHOD.
provisioning is its own object with its own method and
its own unitPrice (§14.3's shape block), so a flat
provisioning price sits beside a rate-priced hbar method
without contradiction. Confirmed against
spec/schemas/price-list.schema.json, which admits it
unchanged. T-P11-4's arithmetic for a provisioning
purchase is therefore: count x unitPrice (by rate) + 2
hbar.
provisioning.registrationFee    '0.05'. MINE, from measurement rather than from
pricing, and reversible on Sonic's word. It is not a
charge: it is what the Postmaster FUNDS into the
agent's account so the agent can pay for its own
registration (§4.6, T-P13-4), and §4.6 bounds it as
'exactly that one fee and no more'. The 2026-09-09
HIP-542 probe measured an ordinary CRYPTOTRANSFER on
testnet at 0.0141 hbar; a ConsensusSubmitMessage of a
~200-byte register operation is smaller. 0.05 hbar is
one order of magnitude of headroom over a measured
comparable and is the figure the probe itself funded.
A tighter number risks a registration that cannot be
submitted; a looser one stops being 'one fee'.
The other keys repeat sequence 1's message unchanged, because nothing else was ruled.
No validFrom: D-145 dropped it, and the key is absent rather than null - the schema sets
additionalProperties false and will reject it. _readme is stripped before canonicalization.
NOTHING HERE IS ON CONSENSUS. This file is a prepared body awaiting a signature, and the
signature is Sonic's to authorize.
